text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Opposition MPs plan are planning to hold a vote of no-confidence against Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi over allegatiions of illegal privatisation of appartments.
- The hunger strike at the Oru peat plant in northwest Estonia continues despite an allocation of funds by the government.

- There were no human rights violations in Estonia, OSCE commissioner Max van der Stoel declared in a letter to Russian daily Estonija, dismissing remarks on ethnic minorities that the newspaper had attributed to him.
- Delegations from 18 countries and the U.N. are attending a conference on sustainable development in Tallinn.
- One of the reasons for the split of parliament's Russian faction was Moscow's attempt to strengthen its influence among the Russian population in Estonia, the newspaper claims.
- Foreign Ministry chancellor Indrek Tarand is one of the many senior officials who attended a Defence Forces course for officers in reserve.
- A mother whose son suffered brain damage as a result of an incorrect dose of anaesthetics, has started court procedures against the doctors involved.
- Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves is planning to visit all EU member countries in the next three months to promote Estonia's position on EU expansion.
